changes.text: 足额口粮只够五个星期，一条小船，六个名额。队长要说服全队走一条危险极大的路，还要否掉带病号上船的提议，并在开船前把整支队伍交到留守者手里。

Full rations for five weeks, one small boat, six places. The leader had to talk the whole party into a voyage whose perils were extreme, veto a proposal to take a sick man along, and hand the stranded party over to the man staying behind before the boat pulled away.
象岛上，口粮按足额只够全队吃五个星期，减量可以撑三个月，或许还能靠海兽补一些，但队长不敢把信心全押在这上面：海滩上的海兽似乎都走了，冬天近了。存量里有三只海豹和两张半带脂肪的兽皮，燃料主要靠脂肪。初步估量形势后，队长决定全队每天只吃一顿热食。

On Elephant Island the food would last the whole party five weeks at full ration. Cut back, it could be spread over three months, and would probably be supplemented to some extent by seals and sea-elephants — but the leader dared not count on that with full confidence. The animals seemed to have deserted the beach and winter was near. Their stocks included three seals and two and a half skins with the blubber attached, and they were mainly dependent on blubber for fuel. After a preliminary survey of the situation, he decided the party must be limited to one hot meal a day.
求援的去处是南乔治亚。它在八百多英里以外，但位于西风带内，东岸任何一个捕鲸站都可以指望找到捕鲸人；只要海上没有冰、小船撑得过那些巨浪，一队人乘船可望完成航行，并在一个月之内带着援助返回。

The destination was South Georgia. It lay over eight hundred miles off, but inside the belt of the west winds, and whalers could be counted on at any of the whaling stations on its east coast. Provided the sea was clear of ice and the boat survived the great seas, a boat party might make the voyage and be back with relief within a month.
出海的风险明摆着。队长算过最坏情形：这趟冒险不会给留在岛上的人增加任何风险，冬天要吃饭的嘴也少了；船上只带六人一个月的口粮——「for if we did not make South Georgia in that time we were sure to go under」，一个月到不了南乔治亚，就是死路。还有一条让他格外看重的考虑：象岛上根本不会有任何搜寻队来找他们。

The hazards of the ocean were plain, but the leader had priced the worst case. At worst the venture would add nothing to the risks of the men left on the island — there would be fewer mouths to feed through the winter — and the boat needed no more than a month's provisions for six, "for if we did not make South Georgia in that time we were sure to go under". And one consideration weighed with him: there was no chance at all of any search being made for them on Elephant Island.
这件事必须向全队讲清楚。记述写明这个案子需要详细论证，因为所有人都知道航程的危险是极端的，风险只由援助的急迫需要来辩护。五月中，合恩角以南的海域被认为是世界上最暴虐的风暴水域，天气不稳，天色阴沉，大风几乎不停。一种解释是：他没有把出海说成上策，只说成不得已。

The case had to be argued to the whole party in some detail, since everyone knew the journey's perils were extreme, and the risk was justified only by their urgent need of assistance. In mid-May the ocean south of Cape Horn is known to be the most tempestuous storm-swept area of water in the world: unsettled weather, dull overcast skies, gales almost unceasing. One reading is that he did not present the voyage as the best option, only the necessary one.
谁去谁留，从两个要求随行的人说起。Worsley 和 Wild 都意识到必须出海，都要求随行；队长当场告诉 Wild 他必须留下，靠他把队伍拢住，并交代万一求援失败，春季带人去 Deception Island。带 Worsley 的理由写得很实在：队长对他的定位又快又准评价极高，尤其在困难情况下能迅速测出并算出船位。

Who went and who stayed began with two men who asked to come. Worsley and Wild both realized the attempt must be made, and both asked to accompany him. The leader told Wild at once that he must stay — to hold the party together during the absence and, if the rescue failed, to take the men to Deception Island in the spring. His reason for taking Worsley was practical: "a very high opinion of his accuracy and quickness as a navigator, and especially in the snapping and working out of positions in difficult circumstances".
还需要四个人。队长决定征求志愿者，同时老老实实写明：他心里其实基本知道会选谁——「I pretty well knew which of the people I would select」。Crean 原本被安排留在岛上当 Wild 的帮手，他恳求随行，与 Wild 商量之后，队长答应带上他。挑人的标准也摆在明处：有人不够强壮，担不动船上的活；有人不是熟练水手，在船上派不上用场。

Four more were needed. He called for volunteers while admitting, honestly, that he already knew his choices — "I pretty well knew which of the people I would select". Crean had been slated to stay behind as Wild's right-hand man, but he begged so hard for a place in the boat that, after consulting Wild, the leader promised to take him. The criteria were stated openly: some were not fit for the work the boat would demand, and others, not seasoned sailors, would be of little use aboard.
有人提议把双脚冻伤的 Blackborrow 带上船，让他尽快得到温暖和庇护。队长否掉了这个提议。记录里给的理由是存活推断：健康的人在船上都难活，重病躺在舱底、动弹不得的人，熬不过必定会遇到的坏天气。

One proposal was to take Blackborrow, the man with the frostbitten feet, so that he could have shelter and warmth as quickly as possible. The leader vetoed it. The record gives survival reasoning: fit men would find it hard enough to live in the boat, and a sick man lying helpless in the bottom could not be expected to survive the heavy weather they were sure to encounter.
名单最后定为 Worsley、Crean、McNeish、McCarthy、Vincent 和队长本人六人。队长把木匠叫来，请他想办法让小船更耐风浪；木匠先问自己是不是随行的人，听说「Yes」显得相当高兴。他年过五十，身体不算好。

The list closed at six: Worsley, Crean, McNeish, McCarthy, Vincent, and the leader himself. The leader called the carpenter and asked whether he could do anything to make the boat more seaworthy; the carpenter's first question was whether he was going along, and hearing "Yes," he seemed quite pleased. He was over fifty and not altogether fit.
拼凑出来的东西很简陋，但足以给一层帆布覆罩打底。帆布冻得硬邦邦，只能先裁好，再在脂肪炉上一英尺一英尺地烤开，才能缝成覆罩，最后钉好、拧紧。覆罩装上后确实给了小船一层安全的样子，可队长心里不踏实，觉得它「bore a strong likeness to stage scenery」——看着像花岗石墙，其实不过是帆布和板条。事后证明，这层覆罩确实顶用。

What was put together was a patched-up affair, but it provided a base for a canvas covering. The canvas came frozen stiff; it had to be cut and then thawed over the blubber stove foot by foot before it could be sewn into a cover, then nailed and screwed into position. The cover did lend the boat an appearance of safety, but the leader felt uneasy that "it bore a strong likeness to stage scenery" — a wall that looks like granite and is in fact no better than canvas and lath. As events proved, the covering served its purpose well.

浮冰随时可能合拢。决定做出后，队长用当天余下的时间检查船、装备和物资，并与 Worsley、Wild 商量计划。在象岛坚实陆地上的最后一夜又冷又不舒服。开船前，队长乘小艇上岸，与留守并全权指挥的 Wild 作最后交代：交代万一求援失败他该怎么做，同时几乎把整个局面和行动、决定的范围都交给 Wild 自行判断，「I practically left the whole situation and scope of action and decision to his own judgment」，并告诉他把队伍托付给他，随后向众人道别。升帆解缆向东北而去时，留在岸上的人在海边站成一小群，背后是岛上冷硬的高地，脚下的海在翻涌；他们挥手，喊了三声欢呼。

The pack might close at any time. With that decision made, the leader spent the rest of the day looking over the boat, gear and stores, and discussing plans with Worsley and Wild. The last night on the solid ground of Elephant Island was cold and uncomfortable. Before casting off, the leader went ashore for a final word with Wild, who remained in full command: directions for what to do if no help came, and then, in his words, "I practically left the whole situation and scope of action and decision to his own judgment". He told Wild he trusted the party to him and said goodbye to the men. With the jib set and the painter cut, they stood away to the north-east. Those left behind made a pathetic little group on the beach, grim heights at their backs and the sea seething at their feet — but they waved and gave three hearty cheers.
有一天上午 11 点前后，缆绳断了，海锚丢失，船突然横落进浪谷，向下风漂去。那是不必冒险在大风中升帆也能让船头顶浪的唯一手段，连同宝贵的绳子都找不回来，只能敲掉帆上的冰，升帆赌它撑得住。航程中一次测算显示：已走 380 多英里，接近南乔治亚的一半。看样子能撑过去。

About 11 a.m. one day the painter parted and the sea-anchor went — the only means of keeping the boat's head up to the seas without the risk of hoisting sail in a gale, lost along with the valuable rope. She suddenly fell off into the trough of the sea and drifted to leeward. They beat the ice off the frozen canvas and hoisted it, trusting it to hold. One reckoning showed over 380 miles done, getting on for half-way to South Georgia. It looked as though they were going to get through.

航程中有一次，遇上了队长二十六年海上经历中从未见过的巨浪，与多日来那些白浪翻卷的大浪完全不同。他高喊大家抓紧。船被像软木塞一样抛起、向前甩出，灌进半船水，在重击下颤抖；所有人拼命用随手抓到的容器掏水，十分钟后才觉得船重新有了生命。Vincent 在过去一周已不再是积极的船员，队长写明难以解释他的垮掉——他是船上体格最强壮的人之一，年轻，在北海拖网船上干过，本该比 McCarthy 更能吃苦，而 McCarthy 没那么强壮，却总是乐呵呵的。淡水减到每人每天半品脱。带上船的冰块早已用完，装船时一只水桶在浪里被撞裂，渗进了一些海水，喝的水发咸，渴得更厉害；队长不肯增加配给，有人恳求预支第二天的水，也被拒绝：万一风向不利，船可能被吹离海岛，航程拖长许多天。原文感叹，缺水是人所能承受的最严酷的匮乏。

At one point came a wave beyond anything the leader had met in twenty-six years at sea — a mighty upheaval of the ocean, quite apart from the white-capped seas that had been their tireless enemies for many days. He shouted for everyone to hold on: "It's got us!" The boat was lifted and flung forward like a cork, half-full of water and shuddering under the blow; the men baled with the energy of men fighting for life, and after ten minutes of uncertainty felt her renew her life beneath them. Vincent had for the past week ceased to be an active member of the crew, and the leader could not easily account for his collapse: physically one of the strongest men in the boat, young, with service on North Sea trawlers, he should have borne hardship better than McCarthy, who was not so strong but always happy. The daily water allowance was cut to half a pint a man. The lumps of ice taken aboard were long gone, and the breaker had been slightly stove in during loading, letting in some sea-water, so the brackish water sharpened the thirst; the leader would not raise the allowance or let anyone draw against the morrow's, however he was begged — should the wind turn unfavourable, it might drive them away from the island and lengthen the voyage by many days. Lack of water, the account adds, is the severest privation men can be condemned to endure.
把这几个决定放在一起看，一种解释是：真正让这个方案说得出口的，是最坏情形那笔账。出海的人带一个月口粮，失败就是失败，而留下的人在冬天少了几张要吃饭的嘴；最坏情形被算成：也不会给留下的人增加风险。作者推断，当所有选项都糟透时，人们愿意跟从的未必是更有希望的那条路，而可能是把代价算清楚、不把损失转嫁给同伴的那条路。

Read together, these decisions suggest one explanation: what made the plan speakable was the arithmetic of the worst case. The boat party carried a month's provisions; if they failed, they failed. The men left behind would have fewer mouths to feed through the winter. The worst case was calculated as adding nothing to the risks of the men left on the island. The author infers that when every option is grim, people will follow not necessarily the more hopeful road, but the one that costs its losses honestly and does not shift them onto comrades.
这套记录只有当事人一个史源，是他事后写下的第一人称自述。文中的对话都带有记述性质：把队伍托付给 Wild 的那句交代、Crean 恳求随行，都未必是逐字原话。队长自述看队员时信心在增加，那是回忆中的自我描述，不是当时可核实的心理记录。

This record rests on exactly one historical source: a first-person account written after the fact by one of those involved. Its dialogue is reported, not transcribed — the words entrusting the party to Wild, Crean's plea for a place in the boat — and need not be verbatim. The leader's statement that his confidence grew as he looked at the men is retrospective self-description, not a verifiable record of his state of mind at the time.
还有两处要留白。Vincent 为什么垮掉，队长自己说难以解释，本文不替他补心理。所引片段未给公元年份，这里不做换算；正文的天数只保留原文明确写出的出海第六天，月份照原文；距离、口粮、水的数字都照原文：八百多英里、三百八十多英里、半品脱。原文是扫描识别文本，个别字词有讹误，引文照原文写法。

Two blanks stay blank. Why Vincent collapsed, the leader himself says he could not easily account for, and this piece supplies no psychology for him. The quoted passages give no calendar year, so none is supplied here; the only day count kept in the text is the sixth day out, which the original states explicitly, and the month follows the original; distances, rations and water figures follow the original: over eight hundred miles, over three hundred and eighty miles, half a pint. The source is a scanned, text-recognized print, with occasional garbled words; quotations follow it as printed.

dispositions.rationale: 删去证据外的“脆弱”和“胜算很小”，中文改为“一条小船”“一条危险极大的路”，英文改为 one small boat 和 a voyage whose perils were extreme。

evidence.quote: all hands knew that the perils of the proposed journey were extreme

dispositions.rationale: 证据没有给出 captain 这一职衔。所有英文字段里的 the captain 都改为 the leader，与中文“队长”对应；对应中文字段同步给出，内容不变。

evidence.quote: who was remaining in full command

dispositions.rationale: 去掉“于是/So”造成的直接因果，恢复原文写法：他先初步估量形势，再亲自作出决定。

evidence.quote: after making a preliminary survey of the situation, I decided that the party must be limited to one hot meal a day

dispositions.rationale: “一支船队”改为“一队人乘船”，与原文 boat party 一致。

evidence.quote: A boat party might make the voyage

dispositions.rationale: 删去证据外的“六张嘴/six”，中文改为“冬天要吃饭的嘴也少了”，英文改为 fewer mouths to feed。

evidence.quote: There would be fewer mouths to feed during the winter

dispositions.rationale: 删去“正因为如此/So”。英文恢复 since 引出的原因：全队都知道航程危险极端。

evidence.quote: The case required to be argued in some detail, since all hands knew that the perils of the proposed journey were extreme

dispositions.rationale: 中文改为“船突然横落进浪谷”，避免读成翻覆；英文同步补上 suddenly 和 of the sea。

evidence.quote: the boat suddenly fell off into the trough of the sea

dispositions.rationale: 拒绝增水的理由只保留逆风可能拖长航程一条。“缺水是最严酷的匮乏”拆出来单独成句，标明是原文的感叹。

evidence.quote: I dared not permit the 175 SOUTH allowance of water to be increased since an unfavourable wind might drive us away from the island and lengthen our voyage by many days
Lack of water is always the most severe privation that men can be condemned to endure

dispositions.rationale: 删去“六张嘴/six”，中文改为“少了几张要吃饭的嘴”，英文改为 fewer mouths to feed。

evidence.quote: There would be fewer mouths to feed during the winter

dispositions.rationale: “风险的下限/floor”方向说反了，改为“最坏情形被算成/The worst case was calculated as”。

evidence.quote: at worst the venture would add nothing to the risks of the men left on the island

dispositions.rationale: 补回原文的“多/over”，改为“八百多英里/over eight hundred miles”；英文同时按 F2 改为 the leader。

evidence.quote: South Georgia was over 800 miles away

dispositions.rationale: 中文补上“天气不稳”，与英文 unsettled weather 和原文一致。
